summary: Phase 2 backend testing (attachments, WebSocket messaging, Excel exports, recurring tasks). 22/22 pytest tests passed. All requested flows verified end-to-end against the live preview backend URL.

minor.issue: routes_ws.py calls ws.close(code=4401) BEFORE ws.accept(). Under ASGI/Starlette this manifests as an HTTP 403 during the WebSocket handshake — clients never see the 4401 application close code. To honour the documented contract (close 4401/4403), call `await ws.accept()` first, then `await ws.close(code=4401)`. Functionally the connection is still rejected, so this is a spec/behaviour mismatch rather than a security defect.

action_items: Optional: In routes_ws.py, call ws.accept() before ws.close(code=4401/4403) so the client observes the intended WebSocket close code instead of an HTTP 403 handshake rejection.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_ws.py: `ws.close(code=4401)` before accept() produces HTTP 403 handshake rejection, not a 4401 close frame — misleading vs. the documented contract.
recurring.py compute_next_run: monthly uses fixed 30-day step (not calendar-month accurate); acceptable for MVP but note for future.
recurring._tick: no locking — if two workers/instances ran, a template could spawn twice per tick. Fine for single-process, but flag for horizontal scaling.
routes_files.py upload: reads entire file into memory before size check (up to 25MB). Consider streaming with a size guard for larger uploads.
routes_exports.py: loads up to 50k timer_sessions into memory to build costs/productivity. Consider server-side aggregation for scale.
routes_tasks.py PATCH returns `{ok: true}` instead of the updated document — client must re-GET. Consider returning the updated task for parity with POST.
